sourcedFrom: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: The BRX1 is a straight-pull, and its whole maintenance strip is one moving group: the bolt carrier slides straight out of the receiver once the release button is pushed up. Everything the book asks of an owner is done with that carrier and the trigger group on the bench.

steps.title: Unloaded — chamber, receiver AND magazine
steps.action: Beretta's demand for every procedure in this book is the same three places: cartridge chamber, receiver and magazine, all empty. Do it before the carrier moves, and keep the muzzle off anything hard or flat while you work.
steps.aside: It is advisable to carry out the assem- bly operations over a table to catch any components if they fall.
steps.quote: ALL ASSEMBLY, DISASSEMBLY AND MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES MUST BE CARRIED OUT WITH THE FIRE- ARM UNLOADED (CARTRIDGE CHAMBER, RECEIVER AND MAGA- ZINE EMPTY).
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Both release buttons, magazine out
steps.action: The BRX1's magazine takes BOTH release buttons pressed together. One alone will not free it, which is deliberate on a rifle meant to be carried in the field.
steps.quote: Press both release buttons to free the magazine.
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Carrier forward slightly, release button UP
steps.action: Move the bolt carrier forward a few millimetres, then push the carrier release button UPWARD. Forward first: the button will not release a carrier sitting hard against its rear stop.
steps.aside: Push the carrier release button upward.
steps.quote: Slightly move the bolt carrier forward.
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Carrier slides straight out — strip complete
steps.action: With the button up, slide the carrier completely out of the receiver. That is the whole strip for cleaning: rifle, carrier, magazine.
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Barrel, and the locking shoulders at the breech
steps.action: Soft flannel through the bore, bronze brush or an oiled cloth if the residue needs it. Then clean the LOCKING SHOULDERS at the barrel breech thoroughly — on a straight-pull those are the surfaces the bolt head locks into, and fouling there is felt in the handle immediately. Clean cloth through, then a light oil inside.
steps.aside: Carefully clean the inside of the barrel with a soft cloth (flannel). If necessary, use a bronze brush or a cloth soaked with Beretta Gun Oil.
steps.quote: Thoroughly clean the locking shoulders on the barrel breech.
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Bolt carrier: rails, central and side sliders
steps.action: Beretta names three places on the carrier that get lubricant and no others: the rails that couple it to the receiver, the central slider and the side sliders. Light film only — a straight-pull carrier runs back and forth in a rifle carried through dust, and heavy oil collects it.
steps.quote: the rails for coupling to the receiver;
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Receiver: spray, clean, dry, then oil the internal guides
steps.action: Spray the receiver's parts with gun oil and clean them, dry thoroughly with a soft cloth, then lubricate the INTERNAL bolt carrier guides — the rails the carrier rides on. Those guides are the difference between a smooth straight-pull and a gritty one.
steps.aside: Spray the parts with Beretta Gun Oil and clean.
steps.quote: After drying the parts thoroughly with a soft cloth, lubricate the internal bolt carri- er guides.
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Safety, recoil lever, hammer profile — a light touch each
steps.action: With the trigger group out, put a light film on three named places: the safety, the recoil lever and the hammer profile. ⛔ And nothing else — the book is explicit that parts it does not expressly mention are not to be touched.
steps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.26-27

deepSteps.title: Trigger group out — and mind the recoil lever bar
deepSteps.action: Beretta routes the trigger-group removal through its trigger-pull adjustment section, and prefaces it with a warning that is easy to read past: follow the steps and avoid touching the recoil lever bar. With the carrier out, gently press the safety and lift the trigger group latch with a flathead screwdriver.
deepSteps.aside: Gently press the safety and insert a flat- head screwdriver into the trigger group latch to lift the latch itself.
deepSteps.quote: Carefully follow the instructions below and avoid touching the recoil lever bar.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — Trigger pull adjustment, printed p.22-23

deepSteps.title: Forward, then down — the group comes out in two moves
deepSteps.action: Slide the trigger group FORWARD first, then down and out. It does not drop straight out and levering it will bend the latch.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — Trigger pull adjustment, printed p.22-23

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Touch only the trigger and the bolt carrier lever
deepSteps.action: With the group in your hand the temptation is to explore it. Beretta closes that door in capitals: do not touch the parts not expressly mentioned. What IS yours is the trigger weight adjustment button on the left of the group — position A is the factory setting, B is 7 oz lighter, C is 14 oz lighter.
deepSteps.aside: On the left side of the group, identify the trigger weight adjustment button.
deepSteps.quote: DO NOT TOUCH THE PARTS NOT EX- PRESSLY MENTIONED HERE (TRIG- GER AND BOLT CARRIER LEVER).
deepSteps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — Trigger pull adjustment, printed p.22-23

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Before it goes back: release the hammer, then check the trigger returns
deepSteps.action: Before refitting the trigger housing, pull the trigger to release the hammer — fingers clear, because the hammer moves with force and will crush them. Then confirm the trigger RETURNS to its starting position with the hammer still un-cocked. ⛔ If it does not return, the rifle goes to an authorised assistance centre; it does not go back together.
deepSteps.aside: IF THE TRIGGER DOES NOT RETURN TO ITS STARTING POSITION, TAKE THE FIREARM TO AN ASSISTANCE CENTRE AUTHORISED BY THE MANU- FACTURER AND/OR TO YOUR LOCAL OFFICIAL DEALER.
deepSteps.quote: Make sure that the trigger returns to the starting position while the hammer is still un-cocked.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — Trigger pull adjustment, printed p.23-24

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Cock the hammer BEFORE the carrier goes back in
deepSteps.action: Cock the hammer and the recoil lever, reposition the trigger group in the receiver, and only then refit the carrier — with its guides correctly coupled and the bolt head in the OPEN position. Fitting the carrier with the hammer or recoil lever decocked damages the parts, and the springs push hard enough that you do not want either slipping out of place while you work.
deepSteps.aside: DO NOT ALLOW THE HAMMER AND/OR RECOIL LEVER TO SLIP OUT OF PLACE, SINCE THEIR SPRINGS PUSH WITH FORCE.
deepSteps.quote: Cock the hammer. If you fit the bolt carrier with the hammer or recoil lever decocked, this can damage the parts.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta BRX1 Rifle User Manual — C6D727/002 P029173/002 (form code printed in the running header) — ASSEMBLY, printed p.13

cleaning.name: BARREL & LOCKING SHOULDERS
tasks: Flannel through the bore; bronze brush if needed
Locking shoulders at the barrel breech cleaned thoroughly
Clean cloth through, then a light oil inside; bore checked clear

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER
tasks: Rails that couple to the receiver — light film
Central slider and side sliders — light film
⛔ Nothing else on the carrier gets oil

cleaning.name: RECEIVER
tasks: Sprayed with gun oil and cleaned, then dried thoroughly

cleaning.name: TRIGGER MECHANISM
tasks: Safety, recoil lever and hammer profile lightly lubricated
⛔ Parts not expressly named in the book are not touched

reassembly: Trigger group repositioned in the receiver with the hammer and recoil lever COCKED.
Safety checked NOT to be in the carrier-locked position.
Bolt head confirmed in the open position, then the carrier entered with its guides correctly coupled.
⛔ Push the carrier forward BY THE BOLT HANDLE to avoid pinching fingers in the guides, and slide it until completely closed.
Barrel checked clear, magazine in, and the action worked several times before loading.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: check the bolt head is in the open position and the carrier guides are correctly coupled, then use the BOLT HANDLE to push the carrier forward — not your fingers in the guides. Work the straight-pull several times and confirm it closes fully and the safety operates. ⛔ If the trigger ever fails to return to its starting position, stop and take the rifle to an authorised centre.
